articles.title: Railway engineering work over Christmas will cause 10 days of disruption
articles.description: London Paddington and Birmingham New Street stations will shut for five days but most routes will stay open Passengers travelling on some of Great Britain’s busiest railway lines at Christmas have been warned of significant disruption from 10 days of engineering works. Work will close London’s Paddington station – affecting intercity trains to the west of England and Wales until January – as well as Birmingham New Street, the UK’s busiest station outside the capital, for five days over the holiday period.

articles.title: Streeting says he began stockpiling food weeks ago amid rising threat to UK
articles.description: Defence secretary says value for money and modernisation key for spending to ‘fight the wars ahead’ The defence secretary, Wes Streeting, says he started stockpiling food and water weeks ago in case of a national emergency, as he talked up the threats to the UK and said his department had already begun ramping up its spending in response. Streeting spoke after the chancellor, John Healey, said he wanted defence spending to reach 3% of GDP by 2030 and 3.5% by 2035; having already asked Whitehall departments to find 1% cuts in their budgets for long-term investment to fund defence spending.

articles.title: Fallon Sherrock pulls off shock defeat of world darts No 1 Luke Littler in live TV battle
articles.description: The 15th amateur to challenge Littler in Netflix stream on Friday evening, Sherrock was ‘lost for words’ after winning £501,000 prize The name of the programme was Beat Luke Littler, and Fallon Sherrock did just that. On one of the biggest nights of the year for British TV, Netflix, too, there was much at stake: not just £501,000 to any of the 20 amateur challengers who managed to beat Littler in a single leg of darts, but also the jeopardy of whether audiences would choose to watch the streamer’s first UK live entertainment event – or the final of BBC juggernaut The Celebrity Traitors.

articles.title: Trump beware: US voters are concerned about government corruption
articles.description: Alleged self-dealing by the president and his allies doesn’t look so good as corruption emerges as a key issue for midterm voters Government corruption a top issue for US midterm voters, exclusive poll finds Voters under 50 probably won’t remember the “ welfare queen ”. But she once embodied Republicans’ claim of the underlying reason for US societal decay: the poor are a bunch of fraudsters. Ronald Reagan introduced Linda Taylor to US voters at a rally during the Republican presidential primary season in 1976. A resident of Chicago’s South Side, Taylor had been arrested for welfare fraud. “She used 80 names, 30 addresses, five phone numbers to collect food stamps, social security, veteran’s benefits for four non-existing deceased veteran husbands,” Reagan said. “Her tax-free cash income alone has been running $150,000 a year.” The Qatari government gifted him a luxury jet , potentially violating the emoluments clause of the constitution. The UAE gained access to some tightly guarded, high-end American AI chips soon after an investment firm linked to its ruling family secretly bought a $500m stake in World Liberty Financial, the crypto company funded by the families of Trump and his chum Steve Witkoff. Rich people facing criminal charges have taken to donating to Trump’s political operations and then seeking pardons or clemency. Most recently, Wanda Vázquez Garced , the former governor of Puerto Rico, and the banker who paid her bribes, Julio Herrera Velutini, were pardoned after Velutini’s family gave a $50m deal to Alina Habba, Trump’s former personal lawyer, and donated $3.5m to Trump’s Maga Inc Super Pac. The first family is also making a killing from the government. The Pentagon lent more than $600m to Vulcan Elements, a rare earths startup, just three months after Donald Jr’s venture capital firm 1789 Capital bought a stake in the outfit. Powerus, a drone maker backed by Eric and Donald Jr is selling drone interceptors to Persian Gulf allies of the US that are under attack by Iran, enriching the kids from a misbegotten war launched by the dad without consulting Congress.

articles.title: Cost of living protests  to spread to Germany and reignite in France on Halloween
articles.description: Activists call for people to make their anger known over poor public services including education and housing Street protests sweeping Europe are expected to spread to Germany and reignite in France on Saturday, with police mobilised to stop potential looting and rioting on the fringes of what organisers hope will be peaceful rallies. Weeks of, at times violent, student demonstrations have rocked Italy, Spain, Portugal, Albania and France, where activists on Halloween have again called for people to make their anger over the cost of living and deficient public services felt across the country.

articles.title: Florid language and long silences: five things we learned from week three of Russell Brand’s rape trial
articles.description: The former comedian and his wife gave evidence in the case in which he denies all charges against him Russell Brand’s trial at Southwark crown court began with widespread media coverage on 12 October. The former comedian and presenter faces three charges of rape, three of sexual assault and one of attempted indecent assault against six women, in allegations spanning 10 years from 1999. He denies all the charges. Here are five things we learned in the third week of his trial.

articles.title: ‘The last fortress’: historic Athens cafe closes as countercultural area gentrifies
articles.description: Mouria coffeehouse unable to renew lease in Exarchia, known for leftwing solidarity, resistance and radicalism It has been the hangout of writers, artists, poets and politicians, doctors and lawyers, radicals and revolutionaries for as long as anyone can remember. And for 44 years, Christos Vanas, the proprietor of Mouria, has let them all in. Every day at 7am, the taciturn former waiter has been the first man to step inside the historic cafe in Exarchia, the heart of leftwing Athens . It is a ritual he has kept punctiliously, opening up the famous gathering place before he himself has had his first coffee.

articles.title: 裝扮成哈利波特，公開質疑泰國王室——他如今面臨34年監禁
articles.description: 自2020年以來，泰國已有294人因涉嫌違反冒犯君主罪而被起訴，刑期最長達50年。

articles.title: 朝鮮「精英」黑客組織是誰？為何成為幣安63億美元盜竊案的頭號嫌疑者？
articles.description: 如果有關指控屬實，這宗破紀錄的盜竊案顯示，涉嫌來自朝鮮的黑客如今已擁有多麼強大的能力。

articles.title: Nigel’s ‘chiselled cheekbones’ make the news – Reform’s the Reformer, digested by John Crace
articles.description: Editor, agony uncle, crossword compiler – he even interviews himself. Our sketchwriter finds there’s no end to Farage’s talents Welcome to your new super, soaraway Reformer . The paper that aims to take you back to the 1950s with all the stories that the mainstream media don’t want you to read. Free to all patriots. And those who happen to have found a copy on the floor of the bus.

articles.title: Storm warnings for Melbourne, Canberra, Sydney and Brisbane as cold front ‘packs a punch’
articles.description: BoM predicts hail, damaging winds and possible flash flooding across Victoria, NSW and parts of Queensland into Sunday Heavy rain, winds and thunderstorms are forecast to hit Melbourne and eastern Victoria throughout Saturday afternoon as a cold front meets warm, humid air.

articles.title: Trump called out Big Oil profits. Here’s how much their refining earnings have surged since
articles.description: Trump criticized Big Oil for making “too much money,” but oil majors have since reported surging refining earnings as fuel supplies tightened.

articles.title: AI is coming to construction sites. But does it make workers safer?
articles.description: AI is flagging hazards on construction sites, but researchers say evidence that the technology prevents injuries remains limited.

articles.title: Riot police deployed to Poland’s constitutional court after judge suspended
articles.description: President Karol Nawrocki seen struggling to gain entry to court building in Warsaw amid long-running row over the court’s legitimacy Riot police were locked in a tense standoff with protesters outside Poland’s constitutional court on Friday night after its top judge was suspended in the latest escalation in a decade-long dispute over the court’s legal status. The clashes followed a controversial decision by a group of government-appointed judges to suspend the court’s contested president, Bogdan Święczkowski, and his deputy, Bartłomiej Sochański, amid disagreements over the bench’s legitimacy.

articles.title: Luigi Mangione’s lawyers file to dismiss state charges, citing double jeopardy law
articles.description: Mangione pleaded guilty in August in federal case in the killing of UnitedHealthcare executive Brian Thompson Luigi Mangione’s lawyers filed paperwork on Friday once again pushing for dismissal of his state-level case in the killing of UnitedHealthcare executive Brian Thompson following his federal guilty plea. Mangione pleaded guilty on 14 August to federal charges in Thompson’s grisly death outside a Manhattan hotel on 4 December 2024. The shocking plea came less than a month before his state murder and weapons trial, which had been scheduled for 8 September.

articles.title: The cursed cruise: how the dream of never-ending luxury at sea became a nightmare
articles.description: The MV Odyssey was billed as the ultimate escape from Donald Trump. Instead, the oil shock caused by his war has left passengers unceremoniously dumped in Cambodia The idea was a never-ending retirement at sea, a continuous voyage around the globe. The promise to the passengers of the MV Odyssey cruise ship – many approaching the autumn of their lives – was that on the open seas they could cut loose from the troubles of the world. But the world had other ideas. The end came in an announcement as stark as it was brief: they had seven hours to get off. They were going no further than Cambodia.

articles.title: Albanese looks for reset on world stage as ‘spot fires burn’ domestically and likely interest rate hike looms
articles.description: The prime minister will speak with King Charles and others at the Commonwealth heads of government meeting in Antigua and Barbuda Get our daily political email , free app or daily news podcast As “summit season” begins, reaffirming ties with fellow leaders on the world stage could be a circuit breaker for Anthony Albanese amid domestic and economic woes, analysts have said. But a likely interest rate hike , triggered by higher-than-expected inflation , while the prime minister is overseas will make his job – and the treasurer’s – even harder.

articles.title: Ukraine’s Zelenskyy praises US over $2.1bn Patriot missile deal but warns it could take years
articles.description: The Ukrainian president called the US decision strong, but added that delivery of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles ⁠could take years The US has approved the sale ⁠of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles ⁠to Ukraine for an estimated $2.1bn, but Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned deliveries could take years and stockpiles were needed now to counter Russian ballistic missile attacks. “The proposed sale will improve Ukraine’s capability to meet current and future threats by improving its integrated air and missile defense capabilities,” the US state department said in a statement on Friday.

articles.title: US cancels G20 ‘family photo’ after Australia, UK and others refuse to appear with Russia
articles.description: Marco Rubio pulls plug on traditional photo op at meeting of foreign ministers after about one-third of countries threaten boycott The traditional “family photo” to open the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting has been abruptly cancelled in the US after a host of nations – including Australia and the UK – refused to appear beside the Russian foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov. The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, pulled the plug after several European officials, the UK and Australia made it known they would boycott or walk out of the snapshot that often kicks off such international gatherings.

articles.title: A top-secret spy mission, a decades-old scandal – and the Austin Powers-esque saga to lift the lid
articles.description: Rex Patrick’s latest transparency fight is over what he calls ‘most open secret in the history of Australian spying’ – maybe even the world Get our daily political email , free app or daily news podcast A campaign to uncover any documents relating to whether Australian spies bugged Timor-Leste to gain the upper hand in sensitive oil and gas negotiations will be a little less secret after a critical win by the former senator Rex Patrick. The politician turned transparency advocate is trying to finally lift the lid on the top-secret mission in 2004 that became a public scandal years later after an ex-spy and a former attorney general attempted to mount a case in The Hague .

articles.title: Retired Michigan teacher released from Russian prison believed he would never be freed
articles.description: Stephen Hubbard said that only when he was being taken from Moscow to St Petersburg did he believe he was ‘going somewhere’ In his first comments since recently being released from a Russian prison, a retired Michigan teacher said he only believed he would be freed when he got new clothes. Stephen Hubbard, 74, remarked on Friday that he had heard many times previously that he would be released – but never really trusted what he was told, adopting a philosophy of “seeing is believing” and “actions speak louder than words”.

articles.title: Alaska prosecutor investigates alleged Democratic plot to confuse voters with second Dan Sullivan
articles.description: Mary Peltola denies knowledge as party accused of recruiting spoiler candidate with same name as sitting Republican Alaska Senate race: what to know about Democrats’ alleged ballot-stacking effort The top federal prosecutor in Alaska confirmed on Friday the existence of a criminal and a civil investigation into an alleged scheme by Democrats to confuse voters by recruiting a spoiler candidate on the ballot for US Senate who shares a name with the Republican incumbent, senator Dan Sullivan. Speaking at a news conference in Anchorage on Friday, US attorney Michael Heyman cited reporting by the New York Times which suggested that the Senate campaign of Democrat Mary Peltola and national Democrats had, in his words, “orchestrated a sprawling conspiracy to recruit and prop up Daniel J Sullivan as a sham candidate”.

articles.title: Meta outlook revised downward by S&P on cash flow and capex concerns
articles.description: Meta has been given a negative outlook by S&P Global Ratings due to the company's hefty capital expenditures and concerns about free cash flow.

articles.description: Binance says a security breach impacted about $6.3 billion in assets. The exchange says roughly $3 billion has been frozen and losses will be covered.

articles.title: Canada and EU announce new alliance open to like-minded countries
articles.description: Alliance for the Future, unveiled at Montreal summit and open to other countries, conceived for world ‘shaken by new storms’ Canada and Europe have announced a new alliance of like-minded nations to serve as both a “protective canopy under which our citizens can thrive” and a powerful hedge against the unpredictable nature of geopolitics, while welcoming other countries to join. Speaking to reporters on Friday from Montreal, the prime minister, Mark Carney, and the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, called the new partnership the Alliance for the Future and said the “deepest possible partnership between Canada and the 27-member bloc had the potential to offer unprecedented stability and opportunity”.

articles.title: Binance hack: Investigators in a 'cat and mouse game' to recover $6.3 billion in stolen funds
articles.description: More than $6 billion in crypto was stolen from Binance, setting off a race to recover the funds before North Korea-linked hackers can launder them into cash.

articles.title: How crypto hacking funds isolated North Korea’s nuclear programme
articles.description: Cryptocurrency theft is estimated to generate half of the country’s foreign currency income North Korea plays by its own rules. The isolated, secretive and autocratic country is largely cut off from the world’s economic system – but when it comes to generating foreign earnings it relies on some of the world’s most sophisticated hacking. Experts, such as TRM Labs, quickly attributed the extraordinary $6.3bn (£4.7bn) Binance cryptocurrency theft to TraderTraitor, an elite North Korean hacking unit that has also been known as the Lazarus Group. Though the link may not be proven yet, the pattern of behaviour is familiar.

articles.title: The AI investing story had a rough week. It may be time to take profits while you still can
articles.description: Traders and investors are sounding trepidatious about the tech sector following a newsy week.

articles.title: Evacuation of civilians begins in besieged Ukrainian city of Oleshky
articles.description: Humanitarian convoy brings food and medicine to Russian-held city where people have suffered severe shortages People living in the besieged Russian-held city of Oleshky in southern Ukraine were evacuated on Friday as part of a joint relief operation, the first of its kind in four years and eight months of war. The city, which lies on the Russian-occupied side of the Dnipro River, opposite Kherson, has suffered months of serious food and medical shortages, leading to warnings of starvation for the few thousand people remaining there, including about 50 children.

articles.title: ‘Amateur morons’: Flávio Bolsonaro’s short-lived ‘president-elect’ claim met with mockery
articles.description: Brazilian media ridicule defeated candidate over ‘shameful’ absconsion to US and bizarre letter with wrong coat of arms Flávio Bolsonaro had hoped that by Sunday night people would be calling him the next president of Brazil. Instead, the far-right politician’s decision to flee to the US after losing the election and – for 58 minutes – to declare himself “Brazil’s true president-elect” , has made him a laughing stock, with Brazilian newspapers and commentators raining a barrage of scornful adjectives down on the conquered candidate.

articles.title: Experts warn AI copyright changes could breach Australian constitution and spark huge compensation rights case
articles.description: Scraping copyrighted material from internet could ‘potentially’ amount to acquisition of property by government, Anne Twomey says Get our daily political email , free app or daily news podcast Altering copyright law to allow AI companies to scrape music, books and journalism could trigger a constitutional breach, Coalition senators and the recording industry have warned, as they raise new fears it could open Australia to massive legal action and compensation claims from rights holders worldwide. The attorney general’s department admitted it was “extremely alive” to the issue, and Australia’s leading constitutional expert, Anne Twomey, agreed there was “potentially” a concern – depending how legislation was drafted – that granting AI companies permission to scrape copyrighted material from the internet could amount to an acquisition of property by the government.

articles.title: 中共五中全會「空椅子」背後：常態化高壓反腐如何改變中國官場？
articles.description: 「這次全會進一步表明，習近平的反腐運動沒有終點。」專家說，「持續施加紀律壓力不應只是階段性運動，而必須成為中共運作方式中永久存在的一部分。」

articles.title: Gulf states must rethink trillion-dollar defence in light of US-Iran war, says report
articles.description: IISS study questions overreliance on American support and ‘overdependence on expensive, high-end systems’ Gulf states are going to have to reconfigure their trillion-dollar defences given the damage inflicted on their economies and the questionable continued value of US bases in the face of Iranian attack, according to a study by the International Institute for Strategic Studies. The report says that in the weeks before the 8 April ceasefire, 12 regional states, overwhelmingly in the Gulf, faced 4,670 Iranian one-way attack drones and more than 1,400 ballistic missiles. Nearly half were aimed at the United Arab Emirates. Although the vast majority were repelled, one estimate of the damage to energy infrastructure cited by the report is put as high as $58bn (£43bn).

articles.title: Beijing Queer film festival cancelled after harassment from authorities
articles.description: Forums for discussion of feminist and LGBTQ+ views face growing intolerance from Chinese state, say experts Beijing’s annual independent queer film festival has been cancelled after what is understood to have been a campaign of sustained harassment from authorities. Beijing Queer film festival, which was due to begin on Friday in China’s capital, is one of the country’s oldest independent film festivals.

articles.title: Severe rainfall and flood warnings issued for central Greece and western Turkey
articles.description: Turkey has been hit by powerful thunderstorms and a fatal tornado this week with more heavy rain expected Heavy rain and strong winds will continue to affect parts of south-eastern Europe and Turkey over the next few days, as an area of low pressure in the region has allowed for the formation of powerful thunderstorms. During a particularly intense thunderstorm in Antalya, a coastal city in the south-west of Turkey, the formation of a tornado resulted in the deaths of four construction workers on Tuesday. Authorities in Greece and Turkey have released severe rainfall and flooding warnings, as a further 100-150mm (nearly 4-6in) of rain is expected this week in central Greece and western parts of Turkey, with locally higher totals possible. Travelling eastwards towards south Asia, strong winds and heavy rainfall have swept across the Indian regions of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh as Cyclone Arnab made landfall. With wind gusts in excess of 85mph (140km/h) and rainfall totals in some regions exceeding 200mm, the severe storm has prompted mass evacuations of more than 180,000 people, as well as widespread disruption to energy and transport infrastructure. The cyclone will weaken as it continues to traverse northwards over the coming days, though will continue to deliver heavy rain to parts of northern and central India as it does so.

articles.title: 幣安遭黑客攻擊：涉63億美元 或為史上最大規模 朝鮮黑客組織被指涉案
articles.description: 兩家分析公司已將事件歸咎於「TraderTraitor」。人工智能調查公司TRM Labs在一份報告中稱，幣安攻擊事件的多個要素與早前和朝鮮有關的事件相似，包括2025年Bybit交易所創紀錄的15億美元黑客攻擊。另一家加密分析公司Chainalysis也表示，「高度確信」該朝鮮組織與這次黑客攻擊有關。

articles.title: 習近平之後，中國將走向何方？

articles.title: Houthis sending Taiz ‘back to the stone age’, governor of besieged Yemen city says
articles.description: Oxygen, food and water supplies running low and massacres taking place, says Nabil Shamsan The Houthis are trying to send the city of Taiz back to the stone age, the city’s governor said in a briefing designed to urge the international community to do more to lift the month-long siege. Nabil Shamsan said massacres were taking place in Yemen’s third city, that oxygen and water supplies were running out and that rubbish was piling up in the streets due to landfill sites being either full or inaccessible.

articles.description: The oil major was the latest to smash profit expectations as global conflicts continue to drive energy market volatility.

articles.description: Within two years, AM Intelligence plans to set up 400 MW of compute capacity using Nvidia's Rubin graphics processing units.

articles.description: Foxconn's chairman told CNBC that AI demand remains strong as the company eyes U.S. expansion and a larger share of the global AI server market.

articles.description: Iran said four tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, while Tehran disputed a U.S. claim that key shipping lanes had been cleared.

articles.title: Friday briefing: Israel has a dilemma - can its opposition govern with Palestinian parties?
articles.description: In today’s newsletter: Benjamin Netanyahu has been left without a majority, now it is up to the coalition to find out whether the desire for change will prove to be a defining political moment Good morning. It was described by many Israelis as the most consequential election in their country’s history. And, as the final votes were tallied, it has delivered a result that presents Israel with a significant dilemma. Benjamin Netanyahu’s far-right coalition has lost its mandate while the opposition has a clear majority: but only if the Jewish Israeli opposition bloc, led by retired general Gadi Eisenkot, is prepared to make a governing pact with Palestinian Israeli parties, which have secured a historic result. UK politics | John Healey has backed away from cutting the cost of welfare this parliament, amid dire warnings his first budget could lead to brutal spending cuts because of a £28bn shortfall in public finances. Patrick Stewart | The acclaimed British stage and screen actor renowned for both Shakespeare and sci-fi, died at his home in Los Angeles after “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia”, his longtime spokesperson said. Environment | One of the most ambitious nature recovery projects ever undertaken in England can go ahead after campaigners announced they had raised £30m to buy an estate in Northumberland. Europe | Spain began three days of mourning on Thursday for at least 69 people who died in a high-speed rail collision , as hospitals continued to treat dozens of injured passengers and train drivers went on strike to urge more investment in railway safety. US news | The Trump administration has opened a criminal investigation in California over claims that thousands of noncitizens are registered to vote in the state, and has begun subpoenaing election officials.

articles.title: A pharma giant is moving past one patent cliff — but another is already looming
articles.description: Disappointing data highlights Novartis' challenge to build its next generation of blockbuster medicines, following a series of clinical trial setbacks.

articles.title: Sinkholes, scarred land and scapegoats: the scourge of illegal gold mining in Johannesburg
articles.description: There is no end in sight for the drivers of illegal mining, while police action appears ineffective Cora Bailey has been encountering illegal miners ever since she first started treating injured animals in the townships around Roodepoort, west of Johannesburg, in 1991. But as the price of gold has soared, so too has activity in the abandoned mine shafts that mark the area. In late September, dozens of zama zamas – the name given to illegal miners in South Africa, meaning roughly “to take a chance” in Zulu – arrived to dig for gold across the dirt road from her charity, Claw (Community Led Animal Welfare).

articles.title: Sudanese diaspora and human rights groups denounce UAE nominee for UN top job
articles.description: Critics cite Lana Nusseibeh’s denial of accusations the UAE is fuelling Sudan war by supporting paramilitary RSF Members of the Sudanese diaspora and international human rights monitors have denounced the candidature of an Emirati diplomat for the top job at the UN, citing her denial of accusations that the United Arab Emirates is fuelling the war in Sudan by supporting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. The UAE nominated Lana Nusseibeh last week to replace the UN secretary general, António Guterres, as he finishes his second five-year term ⁠this year, upending a race that had become gridlocked.

articles.title: BOJ holds rates as underlying inflation aligns with 2% target for first time since 2013
articles.description: The BOJ declared that its underlying inflation target of 2% has been met, the first time the central bank has done so since it set the target in 2013.

articles.description: Israel's election leaves the country facing weeks of coalition bargaining and an uphill battle for the opposition party to form a majority government.

articles.title: China expels a record number from Communist party amid Xi’s intensified purges of top officials
articles.description: The unprecedented number of empty seats at the fifth plenum – a symbol of expulsions – serve as a symbol for the scale of the purges under Xi Jinping China expelled a record number of officials from the Chinese Communist party (CCP) as it concluded a major political gathering , which saw an unprecedented number of empty seats indicating the scale of the purges under Xi Jinping. A record 33 members were expelled at this week’s fifth plenum, a gathering of top officials that takes place roughly once a year.

articles.title: El Niño-driven drought in Papua New Guinea a ‘national crisis’ as rivers dry up and local farms fail
articles.description: As many as 8 million people have been affected by food shortages, electricity blackouts and health clinic closures Extreme drought driven by an historic El Niño is affecting as many as 8 million people in Papua New Guinea, causing a cascade of issues from shortages of food and water, to electricity scarcity and schooling disruption. An influential coalition that includes churches, trade unions and business groups has said the Pacific nation is in the midst of a “national crisis”, but there appears to be “no coordinated plan to protect vulnerable communities from the worsening impacts of El Niño.”

articles.title: Intel plunges on a major guidance miss. What went wrong — and how to proceed
articles.description: Further downside is certainly possible, but selling now won't erase the losses we've taken.

articles.title: Microsoft plans to raise $25 billion in debt as it pursues AI buildout
articles.description: Microsoft boasts a strong credit rating and has managed to maintain positive free cash flow, unlike Meta, Alphabet and Amazon.

articles.title: 中國施壓下姆巴佩道歉，但許多人仍不知道他究竟說了什麼
articles.description: 姆巴佩有關一名「中國領導人」的言論引發眾怒，但網絡審查令許多人仍不清楚事件究竟是怎麼回事。

articles.title: 如何不刻意鍛煉，也能增加活動量？
articles.description: 日常零星活動正顯現出保護健康的強大作用，其效果令人意外。它有助於我們消耗更多熱量，降低患心血管疾病的風險，甚至降低死亡風險。

articles.title: How elections worldwide are testing Trump’s influence abroad
articles.description: Recent election losses by leaders linked to Trump have prompted questions about whether his influence over the global right is weakening.

articles.title: Netanyahu accused of smearing Arab voters to hold on to power
articles.description: Prime minister claims Arab Israeli parties used foreign backing to steal elections, in which his coalition lost its majority Benjamin Netanyahu has been accused of using smear tactics to cling to power, after he claimed that Arab Israeli parties had used foreign backing to “steal” Tuesday’s election, in which the prime minister’s coalition lost its parliamentary majority. Netanyahu and his allies called on the internal security service, Shin Bet, to investigate alleged vote buying and other irregularities in Palestinian communities in Israel, supposedly funded by foreign money.

articles.title: JD Vance letter may offer last chance to avert fresh conflict between US and Iran
articles.description: US vice-president writes to top Iranian security official in sign Washington has not abandoned diplomacy Hopes of averting a major new conflagration between Iran and the US soon after Tuesday’s midterm elections could rest on Iran’s response to a personal letter from the US vice-president, JD Vance, offering to restart diplomacy. The letter, written after predominantly Qatari mediation, was sent to the secretary of Iran’s supreme national security council, Mohsen Rezaei on Sunday. It requires Tehran to agree to make commitments on its nuclear programme at the start of a process that would lead to the opening of the strait of Hormuz within seven days in return for US sanctions relief.

articles.title: Nvidia responds to report Jensen Huang was target of Chinese asset, says diversion allegations were 'investigated and debunked'
articles.description: Nvidia disputed a New York Times report that U.S. intelligence agencies surveilled a person close to CEO Jensen Huang over concerns she could be a Chinese spy.

articles.title: Hong Kong’s leader apologises for residential fire that killed 168 people
articles.description: Blaze was world’s deadliest residential fire since 1980, but some survivors and bereaved families say justice has yet to be served Hong Kong’s leader has apologised for government shortcomings that contributed to a fire that killed 168 people in the city last year, a rare sign of public contrition that nevertheless failed to impress some victims’ families. The chief executive, John Lee, and seven other officials bowed in apology at the release of a report that pointed to “decades of failure” by government bodies.

articles.title: Cuts like a knife: Canadian rocker Bryan Adams trolls Trump with new song
articles.description: Musician wrote a ‘love letter’ to Canada with a new album – and some pointed commentary about the US president Lake Ontario, the vast body of water that straddles the US-Canada border, has gone by many names over the centuries: Lac Saint-Louis, Lacus Ontarius, Skaniadorio, Cataraqui Lake. But one thing it will never be called, says the Canadian rock star Bryan Adams , is Lake America. In his new song Lake Ontario, Adams takes aim at the US president, Donald Trump , accusing him of “breaking the peace” between the people who live on the lake’s shores. The ‘lake of shining waters ’ is what the Iroquois called her It’s a First Nations name – not an executive order. But things weren’t going his way in Iran So like a baby tossing the toys from the pram You can push us to the brink But where the open road divides

articles.title: Brazil’s victory for the planet and democracy: seven lessons from Lula’s win
articles.description: The trouncing of the far right provides a playbook for social and environmental movements in other countries facing elections, including the US, Spain and France Thank you, Brazil, for demonstrating how the far right can be trounced while protection for the Amazon is strengthened. In a world where nature and democracy appeared to be bleeding out in tandem, voters and forest defenders in this global south powerhouse have shown it is possible to staunch the flow. This should provide much needed inspiration and, more practically, a playbook for social and environmental movements in other countries facing elections, including the US, Spain and France. The astonishing comeback victory of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Sunday’s presidential runoff against his extreme right challenger Flavío Bolsonaro has brought oceans of rapturous supporters on to the streets, while also thrilling conservationists, climate activists and social justice campaigners across the world.

articles.title: 巴西前總統博索納羅之子敗給盧拉後，為何飛往美國？
articles.description: 這位參議員離開巴西後，被拍到在美國走下飛機。他在巴西因涉嫌洗錢而接受調查。

articles.title: 香港宏福苑大火報告公開：特首率官員鞠躬道歉，房屋局長請辭
articles.description: 這場造成168人死亡的大火發生將近一年後，香港特首李家超首次率領官員鞠躬道歉。

articles.title: 中共五中全會閉幕：出席委員較本屆初減少四分之一 張升民罕見增選入政治局
articles.description: 專家稱，更好的激勵與監督可能減少浪費、提高政策可預期性，但更嚴厲的紀律約束也可能加深幹部不敢作為的局面，拖延支出和投資。

articles.title: 印中關係緩和之際：印邊境官員稱中國軍隊大批集結並搭帳篷
articles.description: 印中關係原本正處於謹慎的復甦階段，直到一位邊境官員的言論引發了人們對實際情況的新疑慮。

articles.title: One passport isn’t enough for some wealthy Chinese. Here’s where they’re looking next
articles.description: For some wealthy Chinese, securing a foreign passport is becoming worth the ultimate trade-off: giving up their citizenship.

articles.title: 劉延東逝世：「紅二代」「團派」背景，政治局裡少見的女性身影
articles.description: 劉延東的逝世提醒外界一個現象：從吳儀、劉延東到孫春蘭，中共中央政治局曾連續20年保持至少一名女性委員，直到2022年「二十大」中斷，權力核心再無女性。

articles.title: Egypt fines prominent editor Lina Attalah and shuts independent news outlet Mada Masr
articles.description: Warnings of escalating clampdown on press freedom come after Cairo court convicts Attalah of managing an unlicensed website Lina Attalah, a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, has been released from detention by Egypt’s authorities and had her website ordered to be shut down by a court amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media in the country. Attalah was taken briefly into custody after a Cairo court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website, prompting fresh international concerns over press freedom in Egypt.

articles.title: Africa’s ‘unprecedented’ Ebola outbreak could reach UK, says top health official
articles.description: Jean Kaseya, of the Africa CDC, warns of the illness spreading like Covid unless more funding is secured to increase preparedness and possible treatment The “unprecedented” spread of the Ebola outbreak means it could reach the UK and other countries, according to one of Africa’s top health officials. As the current outbreak reached 10,000 cases, with almost 5,000 deaths , Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), compared the outbreak to the Covid pandemic, which first took hold in China before spreading to countries across the world, claiming millions of lives, and ravaging health systems and economies.

articles.title: 什麼時候「豪華經濟艙」值得多花錢？來比較2026年全球五強
articles.description: 全球豪經艙排名出來，台灣長榮及阿聯酋航空分佔冠亞軍。

articles.title: 官方統計：中國「養老」人數首次超過「養小」
articles.description: 分析人士指出，最新數字標誌著中國應對人口老化的重要里程碑。

articles.title: 姆巴佩就「中國獨裁者」迷因道歉 背後的資訊真空與「毛澤東熱」
articles.description: 因在節目中以「獨裁者」形容已故中國領導人毛澤東，法國足球明星基利安·姆巴佩（麥巴比）近日在中國引發爭議，多家中國大型品牌先後宣佈終止與其合作。姆巴佩發表道歉聲明也不被中國網民接納。

articles.description: 中共是否介入台灣選舉？ 這次選舉將如何影響賴清德與國民黨主席鄭麗文的政治能量？捲土重來、希望藉著地方議員選舉有所斬獲的小黨，此次結盟能否在主流政黨夾殺中突圍而出？

articles.title: 「盧拉軍團」的WhatsApp聊天群如何扭轉巴西選情
articles.description: 雖然民調顯示敗局已定，但數百萬巴西人加入了「盧拉軍團」頻道，後者被認為幫助將線上熱情轉化為現實世界的動員。

articles.title: What Marco Rubio’s sidestepping of New Delhi says about the US’s stance on India
articles.description: Rubio’s decision not to meet Narendra Modi last week was seen by some as a snub – but by focusing on business leaders and oil, the secretary of state made American priorities clear. Plus: the artist bringing a female perspective to men’s clothing • Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here When the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, visited India for the second time this year, headlines concentrated on who he met and where he went. The fact that Rubio bypassed New Delhi and did not meet the prime minister, Narendra Modi, during his trip last week, and instead traveled to the financial capital, Mumbai, where he met India’s foreign minister, Subrahmanyam Jaishankar (pictured top with Rubio), and business leaders, did not go unnoticed. Nor did his decision to travel to Jamnagar, the small Gujarati town that is home to Reliance Industries’ colossal oil refinery complex.

articles.title: 武契奇14年執政落幕，中塞「鐵桿友誼」何去何從？
articles.description: 從總理到總統，武契奇領導的塞爾維亞進步黨（SNS）一步步將塞爾維亞打造成歐洲強硬的親華國家，中國亦曾形容兩國關係為「鐵桿友誼 」。外界關注這一親華總統敗選，將如何改變中塞關係。

articles.title: UK sanctions Sudanese military leaders implicated in El Fasher ‘campaign of rape’
articles.description: Commanders suspected of sexual violence during the largest and fastest slaughter of civilians in more than 30 years have been subjected to travel ban and asset freeze Senior Sudanese commanders implicated in a “campaign of rape” have been targeted by the UK on the first anniversary of a mass atrocity that saw tens of thousands of civilians killed over several days. A year after the fall of El Fasher , the British government said it had sanctioned military leaders from both sides in the country’s ongoing conflict whom it suspected of sexual violence during the siege of the city.

articles.title: 住着一群代孕孩子，美國加州的豪宅如何變成「恐怖之家」？
articles.description: 美國加州一棟豪宅因男嬰受傷揭發涉嫌虐童案，屋內住着多名透過代孕出生的孩子。涉案男女被控串謀虐待兒童，事件亦引發外界關注美國代孕產業的監管問題。

articles.title: 觀鳥如何重塑大腦，延緩認知衰退？
articles.description: 觀鳥近年愈來愈受長者和認知障礙症患者歡迎。研究人員分析這項活動對他們的身心健康有何影響，以及可能帶來哪些益處。

articles.title: Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi ‘sounds strong’ but is isolated, son says
articles.description: Kim Aris tells the Guardian chance to speak with detained Nobel laureate was ‘public relations’ move from military leaders Myanmar’s former democratic leader Aung San Suu Kyi appears to be in good physical and mental health but is living in near-complete isolation, her son has said after the first call with his 81-year-old mother in more than five years. “She still sounds certainly all there mentally, and physically she sounds strong,” Kim Aris said. “I don’t think she has anybody outside of the military or the police around her, so essentially she’s been held in solitary confinement from what I gather.”

articles.title: 巴黎騷亂中的三位華人：「激烈的地方激烈，安靜的地方安靜」
articles.description: 三位受訪者表示，暴力事件集中於示威區域，市民日常生活並未受到太大影響。但他們對政府能否平息抗議並不樂觀，甚至有人預計，隨著冬季來臨、生活成本上漲，示威還會陸續出現。

articles.title: India slashes cost of cancer drugs after court rules mark-ups are ‘extortion’
articles.description: Case filed in 2022 by patient unable to afford medicine leads to cap on drug prices for millions who face ruin if diagnosed The Indian government has moved to reduce the price of cancer drugs after a retired bank clerk took her case to the supreme court. From next month, 137 cancer drugs in India will be cheaper as the government tries to tackle the tragedy of poorer patients either forgoing treatment, selling land or falling into debt to meet the high cost of some medicines, which are making large profits for hospitals and pharmacists.

articles.title: Aung San Suu Kyi’s son speaks to detained former Myanmar leader for first time in five years
articles.description: Kim Aris says ‘hearing her voice again means more than words can express’ amid loosening of detention restrictions The son of Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi has been allowed to speak to the detained former democratic leader for the first time in more than five years. “Today, I was finally able to speak with my mother, Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, after more than five years. Hearing her voice again means more than words can express,” Kim Aris said in a post on Facebook on Thursday.

articles.title: 暗影人物：與烏克蘭合作的俄羅斯人
articles.description: 從線人和秘密網絡，到破壞行動及暗殺的指控，俄羅斯與烏克蘭之間的戰爭，正越來越多地在遠離戰場的地方展開。 這場暗影戰爭的許多細節難以核實。不過，《BBC之眼》罕有地接觸到一些俄羅斯人。他們聲稱，自己正通過在俄羅斯境內執行行動，以協助烏克蘭。BBC已確認他們為烏克蘭情報機構工作，但未能獨立核實他們所稱參與的行動。

articles.title: 特朗普治下，美國經濟的真實表現如何？
articles.description: 中期選舉前夕，特朗普一直吹噓美國經濟的表現。 BBC事實查核（BBC Verify）調查美國的通貨膨脹、就業和經濟成長。

articles.title: Indian court orders release of two leaders of Cockroach movement
articles.description: Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka spent a week in jail after defying restrictions on protests in Delhi amid government crackdown An Indian court has ordered the release of two leaders of India’s Cockroach movement who were jailed last week amid a mounting state crackdown on youth-led protests. The two leaders of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) movement, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, had spent a week in Delhi’s Tihar jail after being arrested by Delhi police last week.

articles.title: 華東颱風強、印尼野火烈——厄爾尼諾現象影響世界的五個方面
articles.description: 有記錄以來最強的厄爾尼諾現象持續增強之際，全球各地已經感受到哪些天氣模式方面的影響？BBC首席氣象預報員莎拉·基斯—盧卡斯（Sarah Keith-Lucas）檢視相關證據。

articles.title: 翻看英國統計 為何從未吸煙的人也開始對電子煙上癮？
articles.description: 根據英國國家統計局（ONS）數據，目前有超過100萬名電子煙使用者過去從未吸煙。

articles.title: 普京提議中美俄「三方會談」：特朗普響應，北京未表態，基輔反對
articles.description: 在普京建議三方於APEC期間進行會談後，特朗普表示願意參與，強調會談重點將是無核化問題。目前中方尚未就三方會談表態。

articles.title: DeepSeek被美國政府系統禁用：中美AI競爭繼續升溫
articles.description: DeepSeek的免費聊天機器人應用程式在Apple App Store下載排行榜上名列前茅，其AI模型也被美國科技企業採用。Snowflake、Vercel及OpenRouter等公司都已將DeepSeek整合至其提供給客戶的服務中。

articles.title: 香港演員鍾雪瑩、袁澧林發聲之後，她們親述被性別冒犯的經歷
articles.description: BBC中文訪問了四位來自不同行業的女性，了解言語冒犯是如何在工作環境中出現；當性別冒犯被包裝成「玩笑」，她們是如何應對。

articles.title: 《孤獨的美食家》：一個人吃飯，為什麼能紅遍全亞洲？
articles.description: 開播至今14年，《孤獨的美食家》從日本深夜劇成長為風靡亞洲的電視作品。觀眾跟隨主角井之頭五郎穿梭街巷尋找美食和故事。主演松重豐希望讓更多海外觀眾透過美食認識日本文化。

articles.title: 美沙冬是毒還是藥？從香港經驗看台灣選戰戒毒爭議
articles.description: 台北市長選舉引發對「美沙冬」（香港稱「美沙酮」）與毒品減害政策的論戰，然而在海峽對岸的香港，這項計劃已運作超過半世紀。為什麼醫學界將其視為有效降低犯罪與血液傳染病的「減害」關鍵？

articles.title: 新鴨綠江大橋閒置12年終開通：中朝關係回暖？
articles.description: 連接中國與朝鮮的鴨綠江大橋，在閒置12年之後終於正式開通。近年朝鮮與俄羅斯關係愈走愈近，專家分析中方需要透過開通大橋鞏固對朝關係，也被視為關係回暖的象徵。

articles.title: 台灣選舉解讀：「北藍南綠」的政治版圖是否「鐵板一塊」？
articles.description: 「北藍南綠」是描述台灣政治版圖的常見概念，但近年選舉結果顯示，這樣的區域分野並非一成不變，中間選民的流向在這次地方選舉可能左右大局。

articles.title: 「特習會」後兩架美國 F-16V 抵台 「雖遲但到」的時機與信號
articles.description: 本周五，台灣在2019年向美國訂購的2架F-16V戰機先行抵達台灣台東空軍志航基地，同批次共有66架同型號戰機，是1990 年代以來台灣首次戰機採購。

articles.title: 為何特朗普在國宴上送習近平一座華麗的白頭海鵰雕像？
articles.description: 從紅杉木長椅到DVD，饋贈禮物一直是外交藝術的重要一環。

articles.title: 從年輕縣官到國家主席：習近平41年來的訪美影像
articles.description: 習近平即將到訪美國會晤特朗普（川普），這將是他歷來第11次以中國官方身份訪美。從31歲縣委書記到中國國家主席，BBC中文透過歷年照片，回顧他的訪美行程如何隨身份和中美關係變化。
